sections.heading: Consumer principle
sections.text: The Consumer Duty establishes a higher standard of care for retail customers. Firms should put good customer outcomes at the centre of their conduct.

sections.heading: Cross-cutting rules
sections.text: The three cross-cutting obligations cover honest and fair conduct towards customers, prevention of foreseeable harm, and helping customers achieve their financial objectives.

sections.heading: Four outcomes
sections.text: The four Consumer Duty outcomes are products and services, price and value, consumer understanding, and consumer support.

sections.heading: Products and services
sections.text: Firms should identify the intended target market, design suitable products for that market and review whether products continue to meet customer needs.

sections.heading: Consumer understanding
sections.text: Communications should be accessible, clear and timely. Firms should tailor information to customers and test whether important information is understood.

title: FCA — PS22/9: A new Consumer Duty

sections.heading: Implementation: open products
sections.text: The original implementation date for new and existing products available for sale or renewal was 31 July 2023.

sections.heading: Implementation: closed products
sections.text: The original implementation date for closed products and services was 31 July 2024.

sections.heading: Customer needs
sections.text: Firms should consider customer needs, objectives, characteristics and behaviour throughout the customer journey, including people in vulnerable circumstances.

sections.heading: Evidence of outcomes
sections.text: Firms should not only deliver good outcomes but also understand and demonstrate whether those outcomes are being achieved.

sections.heading: PRIN 2A.4 — Fair value
sections.text: Fair value concerns whether the amount a retail customer pays is reasonable in relation to the benefits they can expect from a product.

sections.heading: PRIN 2A.4 — Manufacturer obligations
sections.text: Product manufacturers should assess value for the intended retail market and review the assessment at intervals appropriate to the product's nature and duration.

title: FCA — Consumer support outcome: good practices and areas for improvement

sections.heading: Consumer support
sections.text: The consumer support outcome concerns help throughout the customer relationship. Service should allow people to benefit from their purchases and pursue their financial objectives.

sections.heading: Relevant provisions
sections.text: The review identifies PRIN 2A.6 and Chapter 9 of FG22/5 as the relevant Consumer Duty rules and guidance on consumer support.

title: FCA — Price and Value Outcome: Good and Poor Practice

sections.heading: Relationship with other outcomes
sections.text: Fair value should be considered together with the other Consumer Duty outcomes rather than on its own. Suitable product design, clear information and effective ongoing support all affect customer value.

title: FCA — Consumer understanding: good practice and areas for improvement

sections.heading: Financial Lives Survey
sections.text: The FCA's 2024 Financial Lives Survey reported that 12% of adults had limited understanding of their financial products and 10.3 million had low confidence with basic numeracy.

title: FCA — Products and services: good practice and areas for improvement

sections.heading: Relevant product governance provisions
sections.text: The FCA points to PRIN 2A.3 and Chapter 6 of FG22/5 for the Consumer Duty product governance requirements and expectations.
